title: Maltodextrin: what it is
standfirst: What this ingredient is, why it is in your food, and the names it goes by.

spans.text: Maltodextrin is a lightly sweet, easily digested carbohydrate made by partially breaking down starch (usually corn, wheat or tapioca). It is used as a filler, thickener and carrier.
Why it is in your food
Manufacturers use maltodextrin as a starch and it is of plant origin.
Labels do not all use the same word for this. Below is every spelling we watch for. Some come from other languages, because a pack made for another country prints its own.
One word on a label can cover more than one thing. A plan may also turn on how much is in the food, which this page cannot see. Read the pack when it matters.
